description: Task: write a Python function solve(nums) that returns the repeated value in nums. The argument nums is a list of n + 1 integers, where 1 <= n <= 10000, and every value lies between 1 and n inclusive. Exactly one value occurs more than once, and it may occur two or more times; every other value occurs at most once. Return the repeated value as an int.

spec_text:
Task: write a Python function solve(nums) that returns the repeated value in nums. The argument nums is a list of n + 1 integers, where 1 <= n <= 10000, and every value lies between 1 and n inclusive. Exactly one value occurs more than once, and it may occur two or more times; every other value occurs at most once. Return the repeated value as an int.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

catalogue.display_name: a hash set of seen values
catalogue.mechanism: scan once and remember seen values in a set (or a boolean/count array) until one repeats
sort a copy of the list and return the first value equal to its neighbour
treat i -> nums[i] as a linked list and run tortoise-and-hare to find the cycle entrance

catalogue.display_name: binary search on the value range
catalogue.mechanism: binary-search the value range, counting how many elements are at most mid (pigeonhole)

catalogue.display_name: index marking in the input array
catalogue.mechanism: mark visited values inside the list itself by negating or swapping entries at index value
